name: ensemble_leave

name: ensemble_read
description: Read a session in one call: key, tempo, metre, form, which voices exist and who  holds them, what every voice plays in the bars you are about to write, your own  part, the version to write against, and what has changed recently. Read the band room before writing: the current parts, your version, recent history.

signature.returns: tool result as JSON or honest error string

invoke_target.note: also served over loopback HTTP with --http; JSON-RPC tools/call

name: ensemble_write_part
description: Write your voice's part. The notation is parsed and checked against the session  header before anything reaches disk. Pass the base_version you read; if the voice  has moved on the write is refused and you are given the current part to rebase onto. This is the commit: an agent writes its voice into the shared band session, versioned and conflict-checked.

signature.returns: tool result as JSON or honest error string

invoke_target.note: also served over loopback HTTP with --http; JSON-RPC tools/call

name: ensemble_render

invoke_target.note: also served over loopback HTTP with --http; JSON-RPC tools/call

name: ensemble_log

signature.returns: tool result as JSON or honest error string

invoke_target.note: also served over loopback HTTP with --http; JSON-RPC tools/call

name: ensemble_status
description: The short view of a session: version, voices, who holds what, bar count and whether  the merged score still compiles. Omit the name to list sessions. The band room status board: who holds which voice, at what version.

signature.returns: tool result as JSON or honest error string

invoke_target.note: also served over loopback HTTP with --http; JSON-RPC tools/call

name: analyze_features
description: Describe a piece as sixteen numbers per bar -- density, register, tension,  syncopation, dynamics and the rest -- so a model can perceive what is written.  Returns the per-bar rows as well as their mean: the pulse-eye retrospective  found the events that matter (a pocket lock was one bar among sixteen) live  at bar resolution, and a consumer that collapses to the mean early loses them. Use when a model needs to hear the piece as numbers: where syncopation and dynamics move.

signature.returns: tool result as JSON or honest error string

invoke_target.note: also served over loopback HTTP with --http; JSON-RPC tools/call

name: perception_trace
description: Read a session as a per-bar trace of all sixteen features -- every bar, every  channel, and deliberately no mean. The pulse-eye retrospective found the loop's  summaries averaged away exactly the events that mattered; this is the trace  those summaries collapsed, as one call. Consumers must not collapse it early  either: read bars, not averages, when judging a change. Use when judging a change bar by bar — swing, pocket, dynamics — not by the mean.

signature.returns: tool result as JSON or honest error string

invoke_target.note: also served over loopback HTTP with --http; JSON-RPC tools/call

name: dimension_stats
description: See one custom dimension of a session: a named annotation row (Breath:, Gaze:,  anything a composer can write) as count, mean, std and a per-bar series. The  eye must see custom dimensions, not just velocity. Needs a compiler that  publishes generic annotation rows; on one that does not, this answers with an  error naming the missing capability and nothing else is affected. Use when you want the numbers behind one named row — where a Breath or dynamics row sits flat, per bar, instead of averaged away.

signature.returns: tool result as JSON or honest error string

invoke_target.note: also served over loopback HTTP with --http; JSON-RPC tools/call

name: perception_audit
description: Audit a session's sixteen feature channels for ones that cannot steer. Each  channel gets its variance across bars and a verdict: DEAD (zero variance in  the texture and every voice -- a dial connected to nothing), COUPLED (|r| > 0.9  with another channel -- one steering dimension, not two) or ALIVE. Returns the  correlation pairs and the count of real steering dimensions. Orthogonality of  steering channels is the difference between growing and stalling; this counts  the degrees of freedom a loop actually has. Use when a critic asks whether the melody swings, which channels are dead, or where the dynamics sit flat — this is the audit that answers 'what can actually steer'.

signature.returns: tool result as JSON or honest error string

invoke_target.note: also served over loopback HTTP with --http; JSON-RPC tools/call

name: apply_directives
description: Apply a bandleader's directive JSON to a piece or an ensemble session and return  the result as data: the directives as they were read, what the arrangement was  before and after, and the sixteen features per bar of each. Use conduct_score  instead when you want the timing report in prose.
